import.nameIsLibraryKey: The name “@{name}” in the document is also a key in the library — references “@{name}” in this document lead to the entry from the document. Give the entries other names (e.g. “@{name}/whole/question”).
import.refNowhere: the reference “@{name}” leads nowhere (there is no entry with this name in the document or in the base) — skipped
import.refNowhereLibrary: the reference “@{name}” leads nowhere — skipped (if it is the key of a library work: this base must use that library — More → Settings → Sources)
import.foreignKind: Entry {entry} is of kind “{kind}” — it will be saved as a copy in this base. Usually you point to the existing library entry by its key or identifier.
import.revisionMode: Revision “{name}”: "mode": "{value}" — no such mode ({list}); works like "temporal".
import.revisionPick: Revision “{name}”: "pick": "{value}" — no such pick ({list}); works like "weighted".
import.docTwice: {doc} “@{name}” appears twice in the document — the second one changes the first.
import.docReplaced: {doc} “{name}” already exists — it will be replaced by the version from the document.
import.removeNoEntry: Deleting “{name}”: there is no such entry in this base — nothing to delete.
import.removeForeignEntry: Deleting “{name}”: this entry comes from another library — it is deleted there. Skipped.
import.removeNoDoc: Deleting: {doc} “{name}” — there is no such item in this base, nothing to delete.
import.removeForeignDoc: Deleting: {doc} “{name}” comes from another library — skipped.
import.changedAndRemoved: “{name}”: the same document changes and deletes it — it will only be deleted.

namesOwned.other: {count} names from this document already have an entry from the document “{owner}” (e.g. “@{example}”) — this import will change them. If this is another reconstruction of the same work, give it a different middle part of the names (e.g. “whole-2”).

import.dangling: Entries point up to themselves or to an entry that does not exist: {list} — in the tree they become beginnings, but a view that starts from entries with an empty field (like “Argument”) will not show them. Fix their connection in the structure.

import.anchorForeignEntry: Entry point “{name}”: “{entry}” is an entry of the Library or the Scriptorium, not of this base — skipped.

import.anchorNoWork: Entry point “{name}”: the work “{work}” is not in the libraries this base uses — add the library under More → Settings → Sources.
import.anchorNotWork: Entry point “{name}”: “{work}” is not a work from the library — skipped.
import.anchorWithoutWork: Entry point “{name}”: no work — the button in the Library will not appear.

import.flowError: {text} Without this the save will fail.

missingBefore.entry: {problem}: points to the entry “{id}”, which does not exist (it was like this before the import) — fix this field.

missing.entry: {problem}: points to the entry “{id}”, which exists neither in the document nor in the base.

kindProblem.labelField: The label pattern uses the field “{field}”, which this kind does not have.
kindProblem.readingField: The reading pattern uses the field “{field}”, which this kind does not have.
kindProblem.refMissing: The field “{field}” refers to a kind that does not exist.

says.prompt: The question text; for “True or false” — the statement, for a flashcard — its front, for a gap — the text with the gap [[word]] (several gaps: each on its own). Formulas: $…$ inline, $$…$$ on their own
says.hints: Hints before answering, from gentle to specific (1–3, with formulas $…$); each one revealed lowers the highest score of this answer by ¼
says.explanation: Explanation shown right after the answer, expanded (2–4 sentences, formulas $…$, sources [@work, p. 12])
says.answers: Accepted answers (text, number, date, gap) — the first is the model answer; typing never requires LaTeX
says.correct: Numbers of the correct options, from 0 (one, many)
says.feedback: One sentence for each option, in the same order as “Options” (empty: no sentence) — after the answer it stands under the chosen one and under the correct ones (one, many)
says.left: Left side of the pairs, e.g. years (match)
says.right: Right side of the pairs, in the same order, e.g. events (match)
says.leftLabel: Above the left column of the card, e.g. “Year” (match)
says.rightLabel: Above the right column of the card, e.g. “Event” (match)
says.show: Long list: this many pairs (match) or statements (many) on one card (2–{max}) — each pair / each statement then has its own card, and random others fill the remaining places; empty: everything on one card
says.share: Name of a set of parts: questions with the same name count an answer to the same part together — the same statement (many, truefalse), the same pair (match), the same word in a gap (gap), the same named fact (fact). E.g. several versions of “Which statements are theorems?”. Empty: parts of this question only
says.fact: Name of the one fact a question without parts asks about (text, number, date, one, flash, order…): questions about the same fact share answers — e.g. “When was Grunwald?” and “What happened in 1410?” with "fact": "Grunwald 1410". “True or false”: the statement it judges (without it — the question text), the same as a statement in “Several of several” with the same "share"
says.items: Items in the correct order (order); tiles of the correct answer in order (build)
says.extra: Tiles that need not be used (build); “Put in order” does not show them
says.alternatives: Other accepted answers from tiles: a list of lists, e.g. [["$B$", "$=$", "$A$"]] (build)
says.preview: math or text — how to show what has been arranged (build: formula by default; order: none — no preview)
says.join: What stands between the tiles in the preview — text, by default " " (build, order)
says.choices: For each gap [[…]] in turn, a list of WRONG options, e.g. [["Satz 2.1", "Lemma 3.4"], []] — a gap with a list is chosen from, one with an empty list is typed (gap)
says.back: What is on the back of the flashcard (flash)
says.tolerance: How far off the answer may be (number; date — in units of the precision)
says.relative: Tolerance as a fraction of the value (number)
says.quantity: Which quantity (number): Torque, Energy, Mass, Length … — then the answer may use another unit of this quantity (converted), and a unit of another quantity is wrong (12 J for a question about torque)
says.createInput: def create_input(seed): … — data to check with (code)
says.reference: def reference(x): … — the result the code is compared with (code)
says.cases: On how many inputs to check (code)
says.tests: Visible examples: [{"input": [3, 1, 2], "output": [1, 2, 3], "note": "…"}] — checked before the hidden cases (code); may be JSON text
says.radius: How close one must hit, in metres (point)
says.drawing: A drawing to move — the same JSON as in the page module “Animation”: vars, sim, controls, rules (with "goal": true — the goal), world (things to build, e.g. a balance), elements (interactive)
says.goal: When the answer is correct, e.g. "abs(x - cel) < 0.5 && y <= 0" — computed in the simulation to the end; empty: the drawing’s rules with "goal": true (interactive)
says.solution: Values that solve the task, e.g. "kat = 45; v0 = 12" or properties of things "w2.pos = 5" — shown after a wrong answer; empty: the drawing’s "task.solve" (interactive)
says.goals: Several goals (expressions) that must be reached IN ORDER, e.g. ["x > 3", "y < 1"] — instead of "goal" (interactive)
says.check: "live" (default) — the drawing shows a hit already while trying, judged after “Check”; "submit" — nothing gives the goal away, only “Check” judges (interactive)
says.explain: Entries shown after the answer, collapsed (e.g. a statement with content in blocks)
says.params: Values drawn for each question: [{"name": "a", "random": [2, 30], "step": 1}], {"name": "f", "values": [...]}, since 2026-11-03 also entries from the base: {"name": "kation", "entry": {"kind": "@rodzaj", "where": "it.ladunek > 0"}}, {"name": "zd", "entries": {"kind": "@rodzaj", "count": 4}}; in texts {a}, {kation.symbol}
says.let: Computed from the parameters, in order: [{"name": "r", "value": "mod(a, n)"}] — the expression language of drawings with lists and entries (filter, map, sortby, choose, gcd, lcm, sub, sup …); in texts {r}, {fmt(x, 2)}
says.require: Conditions the draw must meet, e.g. "a > 2*n" — drawn again (up to 60 times); if impossible, the card is not created
says.core: Key for the topics in “About”: “Check what you know” asks about it once, and how well it is known tells whether the topic is a “gap” (condition with rel "core")
says.about: Entries this question checks: its result counts towards how well they are known, and the question itself waits until you master what must be known before them
says.needs: Entries or questions that must be mastered before this question comes (e.g. “What is an atom?” before “What is an orbital?”)
says.form: How it is asked and answered — this decides which fields below are filled in: {list}

inverse.needs: Must be known before the question

text.label: Answer in words
text.says: The learner types the answer; similarity counts — a typo gives partial points. There can be several correct answers.

number.label: Number
number.says: The learner types a number, possibly with a unit; the tolerance says how far off it may be.

date.label: Date
date.says: The learner types a date — precise to the year, month or day.

gap.label: Gap in a text
gap.says: A text with a hidden word — [[word]] in the content (or “…” and the correct answers below); the learner types what is missing. Several gaps: each on its own; a gap with “Options” is a list to choose from (may contain formulas), without — a field to type into.

one.label: One of several
one.says: Several options, one is correct; the order is shuffled with every question. Each option can have a sentence the learner sees after answering.

many.label: Several of several
many.says: Several options, several may be correct — all must be marked. Each statement counts on its own (correctly marked or correctly left out), the result is their average; each is also a fact of its own, so it counts on every card it appears on. A long list with “How many at once” — each statement has its own card. Each option can have a sentence for after the answer.

truefalse.label: True or false
truefalse.says: One statement; the learner says whether it is true.

match.label: Match the pairs
match.says: Two columns (e.g. year — event); the learner connects them into pairs. A long list shows a few pairs at a time.

order.label: Put in order
order.says: Shuffled items; the learner puts them in order (drags). With “Preview” the arranged items are shown together above the list — as a formula or text.

build.label: Build from tiles
build.says: The learner assembles the answer from tiles (a formula, a negation, an expression, a line of a proof) and sees it assembled right away; there are extra tiles, and there may be several correct orders.

flash.label: Flashcard (you judge)
flash.says: Front and back; the learner turns the card and says whether they knew it.

point.label: Place on the map
point.says: The learner points to a spot on the map; what counts is whether it is within the radius.

code.label: Code (Python)
code.says: The learner writes a function transform(x) in Python; visible examples check it (input → output), then hidden cases compared with the reference solution. Each case has 2 seconds.

interactive.label: Drawing to move
interactive.says: The learner sets the drawing (sliders, dragging) and checks; correct when the simulation reaches the goal.

questionProblem.text: Enter at least one correct answer.
questionProblem.gap: Mark a gap in the text: [[word]] — or type “…” and the correct answer.
questionProblem.number: Enter the correct answer — a number.
questionProblem.date: Enter the correct answer — a date (e.g. 1410 or 1410-07-15).
questionProblem.oneOnly: In “One of several” exactly one is correct — more are marked (switch to “Several of several”).
questionProblem.truefalse: Choose whether the statement is true.
questionProblem.order: Add at least two items, in the right order.
questionProblem.buildItems: Add the tiles of the correct answer, in the right order.
questionProblem.buildSecond: Add a second tile — correct or extra.
questionProblem.flash: Enter what is on the back.
questionProblem.point: Point to the place sought on the map.
questionProblem.codeTests: Add examples (input → output) or a reference solution with test data.
questionProblem.codeHalf: Hidden cases need both: a reference solution and test data.
questionProblem.gapLists: “Options” has {lists} lists, and the text has {gaps} — a list goes to the gap with the same number.

review.nothingAtAll: Nothing new and nothing to change — the document matches what is already in the base.
review.editsNone: Changes to what already exists: none.
review.edits: Changes to what already exists: {count} in {touched} — {words}.
review.gone: To delete: {count} — {words} (each listed below, each can be unchecked).

reviewPanel.title: Review before saving
reviewPanel.summaryEdits: and {edits} of {total} to what already exists
reviewPanel.editsNeedAccept: Changes to what already exists are saved only once accepted — each can also be corrected.
reviewPanel.allOrNothing: Everything is saved in one save — or nothing.
reviewPanel.blocked: Selected like this, it will not save — it would point to something that will not exist:
reviewPanel.goneNote: Deleted entries can be restored from the version history. Learners’ answers stay — they count again when the entry comes back.
reviewPanel.paragraphsHint: Paragraphs are separated by an empty line.

worlds.notExternal: {where}: a reference to another world “{ref}” in a field without "external": true — it will be saved and shown as “In other worlds”, but the editor will not let you choose from other worlds there; add "external": true to the field in the kind.
worlds.sameBase: “@@{handle}:…” is this same base ({refs}, e.g. {where}) — within a base you point with a plain “@name”; these references will be saved but not shown as another world.
worlds.unknown: Unknown world “@@{handle}” ({refs}, e.g. {where}) — no base you can read has the name “{handle}” in its Settings. The references will be saved; learners will not see them, and in “To do” they will appear as broken until the world is found (Settings → Other worlds).
worlds.added: Added the world “{name}” (@@{handle}) to this base’s Settings — references “@@{handle}:…” lead to it.
worlds.unreadable: World “{name}” (@@{handle}): you cannot read it — {refs} will be saved but cannot be checked; only those who read that world see them.
worlds.broken: {where}: “{ref}” — the world “{name}” has no such entry, story or view. It will be saved as broken (learners will not see it; “To do”).
worlds.notStory: {where}: “{ref}” in the world “{name}” is not a story — the detour will show only a card with a link.
worlds.incoming: Links from other worlds: {list} — there they will become broken (they will appear in their “To do”, learners will not see them).

generator.question: Question “{name}”
generator.questionErrors: {name}: generator — {errors} Such a card will not be created.
generator.neverDrawn: {name}: the generator did not draw a task in {failed} of {probes} attempts — {why} This card will not be created.
generator.sometimesNotDrawn: {name}: the generator did not draw a task in {failed} of {probes} attempts — {why} Then the card is not created in that run.
generator.nothing: {name}: there is nothing to draw (params, let or texts).
generator.templateErrors: {name}: {errors} No cards will be created from it.
generator.templateNotDrawn: {name}: for the entry “{entry}” it did not draw a task in {failed} of {probes} attempts — {why}

landscape.circle: The learning order (“Must know first”) closes a circle: {list} — in the landscape the circle counts as one step, and the path and levels skip one link. Fix it.
landscape.noAxis: Landscape “{name}”: there is no axis kind “{kind}” — the direction will come from neighbourhood in the learning order.
landscape.noOrder: Landscape “{name}”: the base has no learning order yet (fields “Must know first”) — everything not known lies on the ring, without mountains.

interactive.question: Question “{name}” (drawing)
interactive.notSolved: {name}: the solution ("solution") does not reach the goal — computed to the end with these values the goal is not met; after a wrong answer the learner would see a wrong solution.

json.courseSummary: Course as JSON — export and import
json.courseLead: Kinds, entries (including statements and questions), card templates, revisions, flows, collections, looks, rules and values as one document. The import adds new things and changes existing ones in place; it deletes only what the document lists with “"remove": true”. Before saving you see every change: new items and deletions are selected (each can be unchecked), and changes to what already exists must be accepted — each can also be corrected.
json.readOnly: You can only read in this knowledge base.
json.aiTitle: Prepare from a text — in your own AI chat
json.aiHint: The app sends nothing to AI. Copy the prompt into your own chat and paste the reply (JSON) above under “Import” — you will see what will be created before anything is saved.
json.sourcePlaceholder: Paste the source text (a chapter, notes, a sermon)…
json.formLead: The form together with the kinds it needs (and card templates, if the document has them) — for another knowledge base or to correct as text. The same “ref” changes the existing form, a new one creates a form. Nothing is deleted.
json.progressLead: Your answers in this knowledge base — card, how well, when, how long and what was given — to keep or to analyse with AI. The import adds to your progress the answers that are not there yet; it changes and deletes nothing and never saves for anyone else.

kindRemoval.fieldNarrowed: the field “{field}” in “{kind}” will no longer point to “{removed}”

kindRemoval.gone: The kind “{name}” will disappear from the schema.

remove.other: {count} entries of this kind will be deleted — together with the progress of their cards.

kindRemoval.noRemove: There are no entries of this kind to delete.

narrow.one: {count} entry also has another kind — it stays, without “{name}”.
narrow.other: {count} entries also have another kind — they stay, without “{name}”.

foreignEntries.one: {count} entry comes from other knowledge bases — it stays there.
foreignEntries.other: {count} entries come from other knowledge bases — they stay there.

unlink.one: {count} other entry refers to the deleted ones — these references will be taken out of it.
unlink.other: {count} other entries refer to the deleted ones — these references will be taken out of them.

kindRemoval.templatesNarrowed: Card templates that will no longer concern “{name}”: {list}.
kindRemoval.formsNarrowed: Add forms without steps of this kind: {list}.

collections.one: {count} collection will lose the deleted entries.
collections.other: {count} collections will lose the deleted entries.

flowCheck.empty: The flow has no steps — no beginning and no end.
flowCheck.noStart: No beginning: the field "start" does not point to a step, and there is more than one step nothing leads to, or none — set "start".
flowCheck.startGuessed: The field "start" does not point to a step — the beginning is {step} (the only one nothing leads to).
flowCheck.noEnd: No end: from the beginning there is no way to the step “End” (or “Return”, “Handoff”) — add it and connect it to the last step.
flowCheck.secondStart: A second beginning: nothing leads to the step {step} — connect it to the rest or delete it.
flowCheck.unreachable: The step {step} is unreachable — no way leads to it from the beginning.
flowCheck.deadEndOne: Dead end: from the step {step} the output “{exit}” leads nowhere — the flow will end there without an “End” step.
flowCheck.deadEndMany: Dead end: from the step {step} the outputs {exits} lead nowhere — the flow will end there without an “End” step.
flowCheck.loop: Dead end: from the step {step} the end cannot be reached (a loop without exit).
flowCheck.reviewEmpty: The review {step} has nothing to check: this flow has no “Question” steps.
flowCheck.threshold: Review {step}: "threshold" is a number from 0 to 1 (e.g. 0.9) — 0.9 assumed.

answerForm.point: Point on an image or map

balanced_duel.label: Balanced duel
balanced_duel.says: A minute per question; after the first answer 10 s for the rest; bonus for speed and streak.

first_strike.label: First come
first_strike.says: The first answer counts — right after it the game moves on; a mistake costs points.

sprint_race.label: Sprint
sprint_race.says: 12 s per question, then straight to the next; a big bonus for speed.

accuracy_focus.label: Accuracy
accuracy_focus.says: No rush: 35 s, no speed bonus; accuracy and streak count.

streak_master.label: Streak master
streak_master.says: Short rounds; a streak of right answers gives the most.

marathon_classic.label: Marathon
marathon_classic.says: Question after question, moving on by itself after 5 s.

async_challenge.label: Challenge at your own pace
async_challenge.says: Everyone answers whenever they like, until the session time ends (30 min).

describe.actionNext: show the result and move on
describe.async: Everyone answers at their own pace.
describe.round: There are {seconds} s per question — then: {action}.
describe.firstTimed: First answer: {action} ({seconds} s for the others).
describe.nextTimer: Next question by itself after {seconds} s.
describe.nextManual: Next question — when the host clicks.

selection.retiredTopic: The source “Topic” no longer exists — there are no topics. Choose a kind, a collection or a list.

sourceAll.label: Everything
sourceAll.says: Every entry of this knowledge base (and of the bases it uses).

sourceKind.label: Kind
sourceKind.says: Entries of one kind — also from a library or Scriptorium this base uses (e.g. quotes, sermons of one text kind); “From” narrows it to one source.

sourceCollection.label: Collection
sourceCollection.says: Entries of a saved collection — a filter or a list.

sourceFrom.label: From an entry
sourceFrom.says: What the chosen entry points to — e.g. a sermon: its quotes, comments, words, places from the plan.

follow.label: Follow a reference
follow.says: From the chosen entries onward: to what they point to (one field or all) — or backward: to what points to them.

structure.label: Follow the structure
structure.says: From the chosen entries down the structure — along the fields their kinds mark as “link in the structure” — to the very end or one level; or up, to the entries they lie under. In “Structure” it draws a tree in the order of places in the work.

filterRule.label: Filter
filterRule.says: Keeps entries that meet the rule: field, comparison, groups of conditions (AND / OR).

filterWhen.label: Knowness filter
filterWhen.says: Keeps entries for which the condition holds — also about how well they are known: this entry, its cards, what must be known earlier, what it lies under, what its field points to (e.g. facts of a period only once the period is known). Without a learner, the viewer’s knowness counts.

learning.label: Follow the learning order
learning.says: From the chosen entries to what must be known earlier (“Must know first”) — down to the very basics or one step; or onward: to what builds on them.

view.treeTopics: The tree grouped by topics — there are no topics any more. Choose an axis (kind) or a field.
view.matrixTopics: The matrix had axes of topics — there are no topics any more. Choose axes: kinds (e.g. Mystery × Area).
view.noKind: This view has no single kind — choose a kind under “Selection and groups”.
view.noScriptorium: This base uses no Scriptorium — add one in Settings (Sources).
view.noLibrary: This base uses no library — add one in Settings (Sources).

visibility.wholeBase: the whole base: entries, questions together with their answers, drafts, revisions and flows
visibility.members: members of its area (and those they gave a link to)
visibility.membersNotOpen: members of the area — the area is public, but this base is not open yet (Settings → Who reads)
visibility.everyone: everyone — the area is public, so everyone reads {whole}

memory.notOwn: Nothing was saved: the entry {id} to delete does not belong to this library.
memory.saveAndRemove: Nothing was saved: the entry {id} is both to save and to delete.
memory.noFiles: There are no files in the preview.
memory.previewPartial: halfway: lower levels known, the next ones mixed (due, recently wrong, new), some forgotten, new ones higher up
memory.noCardIn: In {failed} of {tries} attempts no card was created — conditions ("require") not met or no answer.
memory.templateNoCard: The template produced no card — does any entry have its kind?

anchor.workMissing: This work is not in the libraries this base uses (More → Settings → Sources) — the button in the Library will appear anyway, but the place cannot be checked.
anchor.notWork: This is not a work from the library.
anchor.placeUnread: The place “{locator}” cannot be read in this work’s layout.
anchor.partUnread: The part “{part}” was not read in this work’s layout — this part will point to nothing.
anchor.needTarget: Choose the entry or the view the entry point leads to.

memory.label: Memory: intervals and forgetting
memory.says: Known when the last answer was right and there has not yet been time to forget. A right answer after a week’s break consolidates more than one the next day; knowness drops over time.

hierarchy.label: With hierarchy
hierarchy.says: Like “Memory” — and in addition whoever knows the details also knows the general things they rest on (learning order: “Must know first”).

last.label: Last answer
last.says: Known when the last answer was right — no matter when that was.

store.otherSort: This identifier already has an entry of another sort — not saved.
store.fromSource: This comes from “{name}” — change it there.

files.tooBig: A file may be at most {mb} MB.

holders.loadFailed: The progress could not be loaded.

anchors.name: Name (this is how the button looks in the Library)
anchors.namePlaceholder: e.g. Argument of the whole article · Introduction · Conclusion
anchors.parts: Which parts it concerns — empty: the whole work
anchors.entry: Leads to the entry (e.g. the leading question)
anchors.removeBody: Entries and the view stay; only this button disappears from the Library.
anchors.title: Entry points from the Library
anchors.lead: Buttons “In Knowledge” next to the work in the Library — for everyone who can read this base. The Library saves nothing.
anchors.tabHint: An entry point says: this work from the library (whole or its parts — beginning, middle, end, also several at once) explains this entry, shown in this view. In the Library a button “In Knowledge” appears next to the work — only for those who can read this base.
anchors.empty: No entry points yet. Add them here or under an entry (e.g. under the leading question).
